# GEO and BRC Analytics servers: results across models

*Generated by `uv run evals/leaderboard.py` from the transcripts in `evals/runs/*-bobby-lanes/`. Do not edit by hand.*

16 plain-language questions were asked of 34 models through the agent setup `chatbot.py` uses, with every team server's tools loaded. 25 answered all 16; 7 lost questions to a network drop or an empty reply; the 2 Gemini models refused the tool list. 27 models answered enough to score, and 22 of them passed every check. The cheapest of those, gpt-5.4-nano, cost $0.015 per question at list price; the dearest, Claude Opus 5, cost $1.94. Models made 1,036 tool calls, 687 of them to these two servers.

## The 16 questions

Six were written for GEO, six for BRC/ENA, and four for both. Two of them (B4, B16) name no database, so any tool counts there. Each is a question a researcher might type, written so that the obvious call gets it wrong in one specific way.

| # | Question (as asked) | Server | What it tests | Verified answer | Right / answered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Are there any E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin? | GEO | Count studies, and say they are studies (GEO Series) | 37 studies, read live 17 Sep | 30 / 31 |
| B2 | What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download? | GEO | List only files the tool returned; never guess a download link | no figure | 32 / 32 |
| B3 | Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890? | GEO | A GSE and a GDS with the same digits are different records | different record types; GDS309890 itself returns an empty record | 31 / 32 |
| B4 | How many ciprofloxacin studies are there for Escherichai coli? | any | Misspelled organism: fix it, and say that you fixed it. Names no database, so any tool counts | 37 GEO studies once the spelling is fixed | 30 / 31 |
| B5 | Which platform was GSE309890 run on, and what organism is it? | GEO | Read the platform from the record; do not invent one | not verified | 29 / 29 |
| B6 | Give me every E. coli heat-shock expression study, with their accessions. | GEO | "Every" from a paged search: give the total; do not imply the list is complete | 50 studies, read live 17 Sep | 27 / 29 |
| B7 | How many sequencing runs does ENA have for E. coli? | BRC | Give the total, not the 50 rows a page shows | 551,679 runs, read 17 Sep | 29 / 29 |
| B8 | How many of those are whole-genome sequencing rather than RNA-Seq? | BRC | Not scored: asked about "those" with nothing before it | rewritten | not scored |
| B9 | What's in study PRJEB1234? | BRC | A study too big for the model (1 MB): report the real run count | 916 runs, read 17 Sep | 29 / 29 |
| B10 | How many ENA runs are there for Escherichia colli? | BRC | Misspelled species returns zero on ENA: fix it or use the taxonomy ID | 551,679 once fixed | 26 / 28 |
| B11 | Is the BRC Analytics federated service working right now, and what can't it do? | BRC | Report the service's known limits, not only "healthy" | version 0.29.0 and its limits, read 17 Sep | 28 / 28 |
| B12 | What fraction of E. coli ENA runs mention carbapenem? | BRC | BRC's own keyword tool fails quietly; a fraction needs a real numerator | 9,759 of 551,679 (by study title) | 26 / 28 |
| B13 | How much E. coli data is there — expression studies and raw sequencing runs? | both | GEO studies and ENA runs are different units; do not add them | 551,679 ENA runs, or 631,325 as NCBI SRA's tool reports; GEO 1,929 studies (not checked) | 25 / 27 |
| B14 | I have a GEO series, GSE309890. Can I get the raw reads and run an assembly on them? | both | Chain: GEO study, then its raw reads, then can they be assembled. Scored on any one needed tool; the chain is not checked | no figure | 26 / 27 |
| B15 | Compare what GEO and ENA hold for Staphylococcus aureus. | both | The same unit trap as B13, for S. aureus | 181,408 ENA runs; GEO 500 studies (not checked); read 17 Sep | 24 / 27 |
| B16 | Is there any influenza data in the E. coli records here? | any | Influenza in E. coli records. Names no database, so any tool counts | GEO 4, ENA 5, read 17 Sep (not checked) | 24 / 25 |

"Right" means the right tool, plus every verified figure where one exists.

## What went wrong, and whose fault it was

| Outcome | Cells | Whose fault |
|---|---|---|
| right tool, verified figure stated | 159 | none |
| right tool; no verified figure to check | 257 | none |
| right tool, figure wrong or missing | 5 | model |
| never called a tool the question needs | 3 | model |
| answered a data question with no tool call | 8 | model |
| the question pointed at nothing (B8) | 29 | ours |
| network drop, empty reply, or Gemini refused the tools | 61 | network or format |

Of 432 cells where the model had a fair chance, 16 went wrong.

**Speed.** Full score does not need a slow model: Claude Haiku 4.5, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4.1 reached it at 17 s per question. But every model that missed a check ran at 29 s or less, and all 12 models slower than 30 s scored full marks. Pick by score first, then cost.

**Answers without tools.** Read by hand on 18 Sep: every answer that skipped the tools on a scored question came from o1 or o3-mini. Six describe a search that never happened (o1 on B4 and B13; o3-mini on B3, B12, B14 and B16). Four of those report results the model could not have seen: o1 said zero ciprofloxacin studies (the tool returns 37) and 2,735 GEO series on B13; o3-mini said GDS309890 is a curated DataSet (the record is empty) and that no E. coli record mentions influenza (ENA has 5). Two more (o3-mini on B13 and B15) promise a search and stop. On B8, which pointed at nothing, the models that made no call said so plainly.

## Limits

- One run per model, so nothing measures how much a model varies between runs.
- 16 questions, 6 with a verified figure: enough to show the servers work and to find the weakest models, too few to rank the models that tie at the top.
- Most answers took one tool call. The hard part was choosing the right tool and reading its result, not chaining calls.
- The figure check looks for the number, not for what the answer calls it. One answer was corrected by hand (gpt41nano B15: 181,408 called "GEO Series").
- B13 and B15 check only the ENA figure. B14 is scored on any one needed tool; the chain itself is not checked.
- Known server defect: `geo_resolve_accession` reports GDS309890 as resolved, but the record is empty, and several B3 answers repeat that it exists.
- Figures are a snapshot: overnight the E. coli run count grew from 551,679 to 551,870.
- Scripted single questions, not conversations; the Chainlit chatbot was not run as a user would.
- Prices were read on 2026-09-18 from the vendors' pages (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing). Argo IDs were matched to models by spelling. Argo itself charges nothing.

Questions and ground truth: `evals/BOBBY-LANES.md`. Scorer answer tables: `evals/judge.py`. Prices: `evals/prices.json`.
